chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Khurasani, from his father, from Yunus, who said:

A hadith I heard from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): I do not remember it except that when I am in the house, it straitens upon me. He (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When you bring the deceased to the edge of his grave, delay him for a moment, for he is preparing himself for the questioning.'
ai.seo_question: What should be done with the deceased at the edge of the grave before burial?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) highlights the profound spiritual weight of this ritual, noting that merely recalling the instruction causes him a sense of constriction, underscoring its significance in Shia eschatology. The practice of pausing the deceased at the edge of the grave (Shafir al-Qabr) allows the soul to gather its faculties and prepare for the immediate questioning by the angels Munkar and Nakir, a critical moment of accountability.
